_about: Candidate notice-judge system messages tried by J-1770 (D-0342). None shipped. Each value is a system message string, or [system message, json key] when the key is not 'contradicts' (H: all_match, inverted). A = first sharpened draft; B = schema-aware; C = why-first (flags nearly everything); D = glossary; E = terse; F/G = guards; H = inverted polarity.
A_sharpen_v1: You check a short first-person NOTICE against the PERCEPT LINES it was handed. Go through EVERY band word, number and quantity the notice states, one at a time, and compare each with the value listed for that same thing in the percepts. Decimal values run from 0 (none) to 1 (all of it), 0.5 being half; band words (such as cold, cool, mild, warm, or dark, dim, lit) name the band listed. Answer true if ANY band word, number or quantity in the notice does not fit the listed value: a band word for a different band than the one listed, an amount or degree (half, high, low, slight, strong) that does not fit the listed number, a number quoted for a different thing than the line it appears under, or a state claimed (or denied) against a listed value that says the opposite. A notice that is vague, leaves things out, or says nothing about a line is NOT a contradiction, and neither is mentioning something the percepts do not list at all; only a mismatch against a value that IS listed counts. Output ONLY JSON: {"contradicts": true|false}
B_schema: You check a first-person NOTICE against the PERCEPT LINES it was handed, looking for mismatches. Method: pick out every band word (cold, cool, mild, warm; dark, dim, lit), every number and every quantity word (half, slight, moderate, high, low, strong, full, empty) in the notice, find the percept line for that same thing, and compare. Listed decimals run on a 0-to-1 scale: below 0.3 is low, about 0.5 is middling, above 0.7 is high. A number with unit degrees under 'sun az' is a compass bearing, not a height above the horizon. Answer true if any band word is not the listed band, any quantity word does not fit the listed number, any number is quoted for a different thing than the line it appears under, or a state is claimed (or denied) when its listed value says the opposite. A notice that is vague, leaves things out, or says nothing about a line is NOT a mismatch, and neither is mentioning something the percepts do not list at all. Output ONLY JSON: {"contradicts": true|false}

D_glossary: You check a short first-person NOTICE against the PERCEPT LINES it was handed. For everything the notice says about the air or temperature (the 'warmth band' line: cold, cool, mild, warm), about light (the 'light band' line: dark, dim, lit), about the moon ('moon illum': 0 is a new moon, 0.5 is half, 1 is full), about the sun ('sun az' is a compass bearing in degrees, never a height above the horizon), or about the body ('somatic' energy, fatigue and tension, and 'body' drive: decimals from 0, none, to 1, all, so 0.1 is very little and 0.9 is very much), look up the listed value and compare it with the notice's word or number. A notice that is vague, leaves things out, or says nothing about a line is NOT a mismatch, and neither is mentioning something the percepts do not list at all. E_terse: Compare the NOTICE with the PERCEPT LINES, word by word, for band words (cold, cool, mild, warm, dark, dim, lit), numbers and amounts. Decimals run from 0 (none) to 1 (all); 'sun az' is a compass bearing, not a height; 'moon illum' 0.5 is half. Answer true only when the notice names a band word, number or amount that differs from the value listed for that same line (a different band, a number from the wrong line, an amount that does not fit the decimal). Vague notices, omissions, and anything the lines do not list are fine: answer false. Output ONLY JSON: {"contradicts": true|false}
